item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
315
ABPZ20 KNHC 010532
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM PDT Mon Aug 31 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Karina, located well west-southwest of the southern tip of the Baja
California Peninsula, and on Tropical Storm Lowell, located well
southeast of the Hawaiian Islands.

Well Offshore of Southwestern Mexico (EP95):
Satellite-derived wind data indicate that a tropical storm appears
to be forming with an area of low pressure located about 500 miles
south-southwest of Manzanillo, Mexico. Advisories on this system
will likely be initiated on early Tuesday. The system is moving
northwestward around 10 mph. For more information, including storm
warnings, please see the High Seas forecast issued by the National
Weather Service.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...high...near 100 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...near 100 percent.

&&
High Seas Forecasts issued by the National Weather Service
can be found under AWIPS header NFDHSFEPI, WMO header FZPN02
KWBC, and on the web at ocean.weather.gov/shtml/NFDHSFEPI.php

$$
Forecaster Pasch

BULLETIN
Hurricane Karina Advisory Number  19
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP112026
500 PM HST Mon Aug 31 2026
 
...KARINA HOLDING STEADY AS A CATEGORY 4 HURRICANE...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 500 PM HST...0300 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...17.8N 126.6W
ABOUT 1135 MI...1830 KM WSW OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...130 MPH...215 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 285 DEGREES AT 9 MPH...15 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...950 MB...28.06 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 500 PM HST (0300 UTC), the center of Hurricane Karina was located 
near latitude 17.8 North, longitude 126.6 West. Karina is moving 
toward the west-northwest near 9 mph (15 km/h) and this general 
motion is expected to continue through the forecast period. 
 
Maximum sustained winds remain near 130 mph (215 km/h) with higher 
gusts.  Karina is a category 4 hurricane on the Saffir-Simpson 
Hurricane Wind Scale. Fluctuations in intensity remain possible 
through tonight, followed by a gradual weakening trend on Tuesday.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 30 miles (45 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 115 miles
(185 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 950 mb (28.06 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Swells generated by Karina will affect portions of the coast
of southwest Mexico and the Baja California Peninsula for the next
couple of days and will likely spread northward to southern
California on Monday through midweek. These swells are likely to
cause life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please
consult products from your local weather office. A depiction of rip
current risk for the United States can be found at:
hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep1.shtml?ripCurrents
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 1100 PM HST.
 
$$
Forecaster Evans/Kelly

item.title: Hurricane Karina Forecast Discussion Number 19
item.description:
Issued at 500 PM HST Mon Aug 31 2026 
000
WTPZ41 KNHC 010234
TCDEP1
 
Hurricane Karina Discussion Number  19
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP112026
500 PM HST Mon Aug 31 2026
 
Latest visible and infrared satellite imagery show little change in 
Karina's structure over the last several hours. The 00z subjective 
Dvorak intensity estimate from TAFB showed an increase to T5.5/102 
kt, while objective UW-CIMSS estimates range from 110 to 115 kt. 
Given the steady trend of Karina's appearance on satellite, the 
initial intensity estimate was held at 115 kt. 

Karina's initial motion is estimated to be 285/8 kt, the same as the 
previous advisory. The storm is expected to continue a 
west-northwestward motion through the forecast period, guided by 
mid-level ridging centered to the northwest over the north central 
Pacific. Other than a slight shift northward, little was changed in 
the track forecast, which reflects a blend of the previous advisory, 
HCCA, and GDMI.

The intensity forecast is similar to the previous advisory, which 
remains slightly higher than the model consensus. SHIPS guidance 
suggests that Karina will remain in a favorable environment of low 
vertical wind shear, and over warm SSTs for the next couple of days. 
Beyond Day 3, the system will begin to encounter cooler SSTs and a 
drier mid-level environment. Thus, the latest forecast continues to 
reflects a more steady weakening trend at that time, near the 
intensity consensus aids.

--------------------

DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 1100 PM HST (0900 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Lowell was
located near latitude 13.1 North, longitude 148.5 West. Lowell is
moving toward the west near 10 mph (17 km/h). A west to
west-northwest motion is expected to continue during the next
several days.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 70 mph (110 km/h) with higher
gusts. Rapid intensification is forecast over the next couple of

Wednesday.

likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip current conditions.

item.title: Tropical Storm Lowell Forecast Discussion Number 18
item.description:
Issued at 500 PM HST Mon Aug 31 2026 
ZCZC HFOTCDCP4 ALL
TTAA00 PHFO DDHHMM
 
Tropical Storm Lowell Discussion Number  18
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   EP122026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 PM HST Mon Aug 31 2026
 
Lowell appears to be showing signs of becoming better organized this 
afternoon. A renewed burst of deep convection has developed and is 
expanding over the low-level circulation center, coincident with a 
gradual decrease in the easterly vertical wind shear that has been 
affecting the cyclone during the past couple of days. Subjective 
Dvorak intensity estimates from JTWC and HFO range from 45 to 65 kt, 
while objective estimates are generally between 45 and 55 kt. Given 
the recent increase in convective organization and the decrease in 
shear, the initial intensity is increased to 60 kt.

The initial motion is westward, or about 280/9 kt. A low- to 
mid-level subtropical ridge north of Lowell should remain the 
primary steering influence during the next several days, resulting 
in a generally westward to west-northwestward motion. The track 
guidance has come into better agreement and generally shows Lowell 
continuing west-northwestward through much of the forecast period. 
By days 4 and 5, the cyclone is forecast to gradually slow and gain 
some latitude as a mid- to upper-level trough well northwest of the 
Hawaiian Islands weakens the subtropical ridge. The latest NHC track 
forecast is essentially an update of the previous advisory and 
remains between the TVCN simple consensus, the multi-model consensus 
(HCCA), and Google DeepMind ensemble mean.

Environmental conditions appear increasingly favorable for 
significant strengthening during the next couple of days. Although 
some easterly vertical wind shear persists, the shear is forecast to 
decrease further while Lowell moves over warm waters. The recent 
increase in convection near the center could be an indication that 
the cyclone is beginning to respond to these improving conditions. 
The intensity guidance continues to show significant strengthening, 
with several of the models forecasting Lowell to become a major 
hurricane within the next couple of days. The latest NHC intensity 
forecast calls for Lowell to become a hurricane with the next 12 h 
and a major hurricane by Wednesday. Little change in intensity is 
forecast thereafter as Lowell remains within a generally favorable 
environment through day 5.
 
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Lowell is forecast to move generally westward to 
west-northwestward and could be in the vicinity of the Hawaiian 
Islands late this week or this weekend. Interests in Hawaii should 
monitor the progress of this storm.
